prompt: Which statement describes honor?
options: It binds professionals to consistently strive to do their very best in every task they accept
It demands putting Army values above self-interest and personal comfort or self-preservation
It commits a soldier to a life of service, the highest value a Filipino soldier acquires
It enables the leader to better care for soldiers, their families, and the community
explanation: Page 18 states that honor demands putting Army values above self-interest, personal comfort or self-preservation.

prompt: Which statement describes patriotism?
options: It is the moral compass for character and personal conduct for all members of the Army, in and out of uniform
It commits a soldier to a life of service, the highest value that a Filipino soldier acquires
It stresses professionalism and excellence in the accomplishment of the mission and the tasks assigned
It is the ability to identify with another person's feelings and emotions
explanation: Page 19 states that patriotism commits a soldier to a life of service, the highest value that a Filipino soldier acquires.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT part of the lesson's description of duty?
options: Professionalism and excellence in carrying out assigned work
Initiative and mission accomplishment
Conscientiousness in fulfilling the obligation
Love of country and loyalty to the Constitution
explanation: Page 20 describes duty with professionalism, initiative, mission accomplishment and conscientiousness; allegiance to the Constitution belongs to patriotism on page 19.

prompt: Which statement describes how empathy benefits the Army leader?
options: It enables the leader to better care for soldiers, their families, and the community
It enables the leader to sustain the will to win and do what is right with pride
It helps soldiers control doubt and reduces anxiety in the team during combat
It allows the leader to assess a situation and draw feasible conclusions from it
explanation: Page 21 states that empathy enables the Army leader to better care for soldiers, their families and the community.

prompt: A leader shows unrelenting and consistent determination to do what is right and does it with pride. Which element of Character is this?
options: Warrior ethos
Empathy toward soldiers and their families
Honor as the moral compass of the Army
Duty to fulfil one's obligation
explanation: Page 22 describes the warrior ethos as unrelenting and consistent determination to do what is right and do it with pride.

prompt: Which list gives the three elements of the leader's Character?
options: Army Core Values, resilience, and warrior ethos
Army Core Values, empathy, and warrior ethos
Honor, empathy, and warrior ethos
Army Core Values, empathy, and sound judgment
explanation: Page 16 lists the Army Core Values, empathy and the warrior ethos as the elements of character.

prompt: A leader wears the appropriate uniform with pride and projects a professional image of authority. Which component of presence is this?
options: Health and physical fitness before deployment
Confidence that reduces team anxiety
Military and professional bearing
Resilience in recovering from setbacks
explanation: Page 26 states that leaders must know how to wear the appropriate uniform with pride, which is military and professional bearing.

prompt: Combat operations in difficult terrain and extreme climates make which component of presence especially important?
options: Military and professional bearing
Confidence
Health and physical fitness
Resilience
explanation: Page 27 links difficult terrain and extreme climates to health and physical fitness.

prompt: In combat, a leader helps soldiers control doubt and reduces team anxiety. Which component of presence is this?
options: Confidence
Resilience
Military and professional bearing
Health and physical fitness
explanation: Page 28 states that in combat confident leaders help soldiers control doubt and reduce team anxiety.

prompt: On what does a leader's resilience rest?
options: A commanding presence and a professional image of authority
Physical fitness developed before deployment to combat operations
Will, the inner drive that compels the leader to keep going
Confidence that spreads through the whole organization in dire situations
explanation: Page 29 states that resilience rests on will, the inner drive that compels leaders to keep going.

prompt: Which statement distinguishes confidence from resilience?
options: Confidence is the capacity to recover quickly from setbacks, while resilience helps soldiers control doubt and anxiety
Confidence is the image a leader projects in uniform, while resilience is physical conditioning before deployment
Confidence is a mental tendency to adapt to change, while resilience is the ability to introduce something new
Confidence helps soldiers control doubt and reduces team anxiety; resilience is the capacity to recover quickly from setbacks
explanation: Pages 28 and 29 give these two definitions.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT a component of the leader's presence?
options: Resilience
Confidence
Interpersonal tact
Health and physical fitness
explanation: Page 31 lists four components of presence; interpersonal tact is an intellect component on page 36.

prompt: Both bearing and confidence are components of presence. Which statement fits bearing rather than confidence?
options: Knowing how to wear the appropriate uniform with pride
Helping soldiers control doubt in combat
Reducing team anxiety through the leader's example
Being contagious in dire situations and permeating the organization
explanation: Page 26 ties uniform and professional image to bearing, while page 28 ties doubt, anxiety and contagion to confidence.

prompt: A leader anticipates and adapts to uncertain or changing situations. Which intellect component is this?
options: Mental agility
Sound judgment
Innovation
Domain knowledge
explanation: Page 34 defines mental agility as a tendency to anticipate or adapt to uncertain or changing situations.

prompt: Which statement describes sound judgment rather than mental agility?
options: Flexibility of mind to adapt to uncertain situations in the field
A tendency to anticipate or adapt to uncertain or changing situations
The ability to introduce something new to the unit and its training
Capacity to assess situations to draw feasible conclusions
explanation: Page 34 defines sound judgment as the capacity to assess situations to draw feasible conclusions.

prompt: Creative thinking in innovation is described as developing what?
options: Feasible conclusions from assessed situations
A professional image of authority
Logical assumptions in many areas
New ideas and ways to challenge subordinates
explanation: Page 35 states that creative thinking is developing new ideas and ways to challenge subordinates.

prompt: Which list gives the three parts of interpersonal tact?
options: Knowing what others perceive, recognizing diversity, and drawing feasible conclusions
Knowing what others perceive, recognizing diversity, and displaying self-control
Anticipating change, recognizing diversity, and displaying self-control
Knowing what others perceive, introducing new ideas, and displaying self-control
explanation: Page 36 defines interpersonal tact as knowing what others perceive, recognizing diversity and displaying self-control.

prompt: Domain knowledge is a product of which of the following?
options: Flexible thinking and adaptation to uncertain or changing situations
Assessment of situations to draw feasible conclusions for action
Possessed facts, beliefs, and logical assumptions in many areas
New ideas and ways to challenge subordinates in the unit
explanation: Page 36 defines domain knowledge as a product of possessed facts, beliefs and logical assumptions in many areas.

prompt: Which list gives the five components of the leader's intellect?
options: Mental agility, sound judgment, innovation, interpersonal tact, empathy
Mental agility, sound judgment, innovation, resilience, domain knowledge
Mental agility, confidence, innovation, interpersonal tact, domain knowledge
Mental agility, sound judgment, innovation, interpersonal tact, domain knowledge
explanation: Page 33 lists these five components of the leader's intellect.

prompt: Which statement distinguishes empathy from interpersonal tact?
options: Empathy is an intellect component that recognizes diversity, while tact is an element of character
Empathy is seeing another person's point of view, while tact includes recognizing diversity and displaying self-control
Tact is seeing another person's point of view, while empathy includes recognizing diversity and self-control
Both mean the ability to anticipate and adapt to changing situations
explanation: Page 21 defines empathy as seeing from another's point of view; page 36 defines interpersonal tact.
